content: Tecovirimat is a weak inhibitor of the enzymes CYP2C8 and CYP2C19. It can decrease the levels or effects of etravirine by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended when co-administered. Tecovirimat acts as a weak inducer of CYP3A4, necessitating the monitoring of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates to ensure therapeutic effectiveness. Tecovirimat reduces the levels or effects of everolimus, exemestane, felbamate, felodipine, fenofibrate, fenofibrate micronized, fenofibric acid, fentanyl (including intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal forms), flurazepam, flutamide, fosamprenavir, fosaprepitant, fostamatinib, gefitinib, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, guanfacine, haloperidol, hydrocodone, hydroxyprogesterone caproate, ibrutinib, idelalisib, imatinib, indinavir, irinotecan (including liposomal forms), isavuconazonium sulfate, isosorbide dinitrate, isosorbide mononitrate, ixabepilone, ixazomib, ketamine, lacosamide, lapatinib, levomilnacipran, levonorgestrel (oral), linagliptin, lomitapide, lopinavir, losartan, lovastatin, lumefantrine, and lurasidone by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised in all these cases, as Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be monitored for effectiveness when co-administered. Tecovirimat increases the levels or effects of flibanserin, fosphenytoin, lansoprazole, isotretinoin, and imipramine by affecting CYP2C19-mediated metabolism. It is a weak inhibitor of CYP2C8 and CYP2C19, and monitoring for adverse effects is recommended when co-administered with sensitive substrates of these enzymes. Lanthanum carbonate increases Tecovirimat levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. Similarly, phosphate binders increase the bioavailability and exposure of Tecovirimat. In all cases, careful monitoring of drug levels and therapeutic effects is essential to ensure safety and efficacy when Tecovirimat is co-administered with other medications.
